title: MELD: A Protocol for Merging Knowledge Across Distributed Agentic Memories
abstract: arXiv:2608.16357v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Autonomous agents share a transport and can call each other's tools, but they cannot share what they know: no protocol lets two agents' memories reconcile a fact phrased two ways, link related facts held apart, or reconcile contradictory knowledge without silently discarding either claim. We present MELD, a self-managing coherence mechanism for a federation of agent memories whose run-time model is the knowledge graph itself. Each brain admits every incoming claim through a five-outcome procedure (insert, merge, relate, conflict, or reject), decided from three signals (scoped claim-key identity, embedding similarity, and a natural-language-inference verdict) under context and freshness gates, and acting through exactly one auditable, authenticated Patch, the only object that mutates state. A binding onto standard publish/subscribe transport with a per-claim status CRDT keeps sovereign brains coherent in claim status without a coordinat

translated_title: MELD：一种跨分布式智能体记忆合并知识的协议
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.16357v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：自主智能体共享传输通道，可以调用彼此的工具，但它们无法共享所知内容：没有协议能让两个智能体的记忆以两种方式表述同一事实，关联分散的相关事实，或在不清除任一主张的情况下协调矛盾知识。我们提出MELD，一种用于智能体记忆联合体的自管理一致性机制，其运行时模型即知识图谱本身。每个“大脑”通过五结果程序（插入、合并、关联、冲突或拒绝）接纳每个传入主张，该程序由三个信号（作用域声明键标识、嵌入相似度和自然语言推断结论）在上下文和新鲜度门控下决定，并通过恰好一个可审计、可认证的补丁（Patch）执行，这是唯一能改变状态的对象。对标准发布/订阅传输的绑定，配合每声明状态的CRDT，使各主权大脑在声明状态上保持一致，无需协调器。
tldr: MELD是一种协议，通过五结果决策机制和可审计补丁，使分布式智能体记忆能自动合并、关联或协调知识，而无需中心协调器。
en_tdlr: MELD is a protocol that enables distributed agent memories to automatically merge, relate, or reconcile knowledge through a five-outcome decision mechanism and auditable patches, without requiring a central coordinator.
